$comment: Reviewed nav-graph corrections for Trades Hall Glasgow.
The forge's KNN graph is same-floor by construction, so the ONLY way two
storeys join is an explicit, human-reviewed link in this file. Until it was
written the bundle shipped as two islands - 84 viewpoints upstairs and 65
down, with no edge between them - so no visitor could walk between the
floors at all. The route finder returned 'unreachable' and the Usher
teleported, which is why nobody noticed.
scan_080 <-> scan_081 is the grand staircase's lower flight, confirmed by
looking at the capture rather than by geometry alone:
- scan_081 stands at the FOOT of the flight, facing up a run of stone
treads with brass nosings between mahogany panelling, toward a pair of
dark panelled doors at the head.
- scan_080 stands AT those doors, on the same stone floor with the same
brass-and-blue nosing detail - the head of that same flight.
- Geometry agrees: 3.73 m of run for 1.29 m of rise, 3.94 m apart in 3D,
well inside the graph's existing edge lengths (max 6.58 m). They are
also consecutive in capture order: the operator walked from one to the
other.
REJECTED candidates, recorded so nobody re-proposes them:
- scan_057 <-> scan_119 (2.97 m apart, 0.04 m of it horizontal): the same
plan position on two storeys, with a floor slab between. Linking it
would walk a guest down through the floor.
- scan_078 <-> scan_140 (2.83 m run, 1.66 m rise - stair-SHAPED, and
still wrong): scan_078 is mid-staircase but scan_140 is inside a
furnished room, so the link would cross a wall. Geometry narrows the
search; only the photographs decide.
